title: playing
description: Playing is the two-party boundary faculty of an agent: engaging a second party across a bounded arena. Formally, the interaction of two dual strategies — Girard's cut, Design ⊗ Design^⊥ → Interaction (Locus Solum, 2001; implemented as @red-cup-engineering/playing). An instance describes one such engagement. The design carrier itself is engineering custody; this schema names the engagement's shape, not the design's internals.

twoParty.description: Playing is intrinsically two-party: it acts through a second party (opponent, partner, world), unlike the one-party faculties.

proponent.description: The playing agent's strategy — a design: a polarized valuation over a tree of loci, carried by @red-cup-engineering/playing.

opponent.description: The dual strategy (Design^⊥) — the second party's side of the engagement; duality swaps Proponent/Opponent polarity.

arena.description: The bounded space of engagement — the shared loci; culturally, the magic circle.

interaction.description: The cut of the two designs: converges when the interaction reaches the daimon (orthogonality) or fails to.

converged.description: Orthogonality verdict: did the interaction reach the daimon ⊤?

lusory.description: Whether the engagement is held under the lusory attitude — constraints accepted because they make the activity possible (Suits 1978). See ./play.schema.json for the play qualities.
